Centro storico — Parma, Italy

🟡 Local-source safety assessment · 13 areas reviewed individually Methodology →

Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

Piazza Garibaldi, the Duomo and Baptistery, the Pilotta — compact, walkable and busy. The figure in circulation is that around 60% of the city's recorded incidents fall in the historic centre, from a map of 700 episodes in eight months compiled by the Vignali opposition group on the council; the majority publicly dismissed it as propaganda, and it is worth adding that the centre is also where nearly all of Parma's footfall is, so a concentration there is partly arithmetic. Ordinary evening care rather than avoidance.

Frequently asked questions

Is Centro storico safe?

Wandroz currently rates Centro storico in Parma as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Parma during the day and roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Parma at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Parma publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is Centro storico safe at night?

At night, Centro storico is rated as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Parma. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Centro storico a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Centro storico's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Parma) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
